next_check: Obtain higher angular resolution eclipse photometry or a precision timing model if characterization is desired.

period_interpretation: local consecutive dip spacing; orbital doubling unresolved
evidence: Sharp repeatable dips in S63/64 yield local consecutive sharp-minimum spacing 3.19139 d from the first six clean S64 events, vastly different from the 58.97741 d Gaia orbit. Stacked TESScut deficit centroid is only 0.19 pixel (~4 arcsec) from target, with a target-centered deficit at TESS resolution (no PSF fit performed). Disappearance in other apertures alone does not refute target attribution. Real repeated eclipse-like events are probable short-period by-catch rather than an established eclipse of the selected Gaia orbit.
limitations: Unresolved neighbor remains possible because complete capable-neighbor cone queries failed. Same-kind versus opposite-kind doubling and long-baseline ephemeris have not been resolved. DSCT/GDOR/SXPHE catalogue variability does not itself explain these sharp deficits.
next_check: Resolve close blends and obtain repeated independent source photometry; fit both eclipse kinds before assigning orbital period.

next_check: Model the smooth variability before making any eclipse search or orbital association.

evidence: The S8/34 candidate minima are smooth depressions between broad variable humps; S7/61/88 show the same continuously evolving baseline structure without a convincing detached repeated eclipse. The 44.78037 d screen cue is not a measured eclipse period.

next_check: Use a variability model and targeted photometry if a residual eclipse remains.

evidence: S44/S45 have convincing 1.90/1.88 d flat-bottomed events with trapezoid centers 2505.65630/2542.17602 BTJD, depth 8.58/8.41 ppt. A compatible S72 notch at 3272.3503 is highly baseline dependent; cycles 0,1,21 give descriptive P36.50930 d using conservative timing allowances 0.03,0.03,0.15 d. S46 late partial primary ingress is supporting morphology, not a timing. Its singular covariance is excluded. S44 independent custom aperture shows 7.73 ppt and a target-centered deficit. Integer divisors 2-10 were checked against actual coverage, but P/2 remains viable: the S46 intermediate window has an actual ~8.8 ppt notch and the S71 intermediate window is ramp dominated, not a clean null. The notch alone cannot establish opposite-kind identity. Only S44/S45 are secure complete events; S72 and partial S46 cannot establish a unique same-kind clock. The plausible tier retains strong real eclipse-like variability while withholding a system/clock association. Full Gaia covariance predicts conjunction B about 2.46 d early (95%offset[0.99,3.93]d), a material~3sigma tension despite broad period agreement.
limitations: Complete capable-neighbor inventory remains unknown after two failed Gaia requests. S72 duration 1.21 d differs from earlier 1.9 d and lies on steep trend; model-dependent late timing and Gaia geometry prevent confirmation. Neither 36.50930 d nor its half is a unique orbital-period solution. No formal precision error is claimed.
next_check: Resolve capable close neighbors, obtain source-specific eclipse photometry, and test whether Gaia orbit bias or another binary explains the phase offset.
